meaning: baseline apparent permeability of a hydrophilic 2-4 kDa peptide; median CALIBRATED to the Seeker baseline
basis: Calibrated so that the median of the reference arm R1 equals 1.2 % (mid-point of the 1-2 % enhancer-tablet range, Brayden et al. 2020; oral semaglutide 0.8 %, Overgaard et al. 2021). Dispersion: author assumption.

meaning: luminal proteolysis rate in the niche without protection
basis: Author assumption (no direct measurement for an enhancer niche); order of 1 h^-1 for luminal proteolysis of an unprotected peptide.

meaning: survival after apical entry (intra-enterocyte handling, first pass)
basis: Author assumption (intra-enterocyte handling and first pass).

meaning: Caco-2 efflux ratio if the peptide is an efflux substrate
basis: Caco-2 bidirectional efflux ratios for P-glycoprotein substrates, order of magnitude (Collnot et al. 2006); applies only if the peptide is a substrate.

meaning: probability that the peptide is an efflux substrate (scenario axis)
basis: Scenario axis, not a prior (peptide-specific; unknown for any given 2-4 kDa peptide).

meaning: mucosal contact area of the niche
basis: Author assumption: mucosal contact area of the tablet niche.

meaning: PE concentration for half-maximal permeability enhancement (millimolar PE activity, Maher 2016; Twarog 2019)
basis: Millimolar range of SNAC and sodium caprate effective concentrations (Maher et al. 2016; Twarog et al. 2019).

meaning: maximal fold-increase of peptide permeability by the PE
basis: Author assumption (maximal fold-increase of peptide permeability).

meaning: PE concentration for half-maximal epithelial damage
basis: Author assumption (half-damage concentration of the enhancer).

meaning: epithelial recovery time after PE falls below threshold
basis: Author assumption (epithelial recovery time after enhancer clearance).

meaning: efflux-modulator potency (piperine 15-74 uM in Caco-2, Bhardwaj 2002; TPGS sub-mM, Collnot 2006)
basis: Piperine 15-74 uM in Caco-2 (Bhardwaj et al. 2002); TPGS sub-millimolar (Collnot et al. 2006); wide dispersion.
